claims.text: Applying an approximately 5–10 nm WC interphase coating to tungsten particles will reduce thermal boundary resistance at the W–Cu interface.
The WC interphase will enhance phonon transmission across the tungsten–copper interface.
The WC interphase will enhance electron transmission across the tungsten–copper interface.
Reduced interfacial thermal resistance will increase the effective thermal conductivity of the W–Cu composite.
A 5–10 nm WC coating can be deposited uniformly on tungsten particles by ALD or PVD before copper infiltration.
The WC coating provides a graded interface between tungsten and copper.
The WC interphase mediates the mismatch in vibrational spectra between tungsten and copper.
The WC interphase serves as a mechanically robust bonding layer.
The WC interphase serves as an irradiation-resistant bonding layer.
Carbon–tungsten bonding in WC adjusts the mismatch in phonon energy modes between tungsten and copper.
Carbon–tungsten bonding in WC adjusts the mismatch in electron energy modes between tungsten and copper.
The inherent hardness of WC helps preserve the composite's mechanical integrity under stress.
The irradiation stability of WC helps preserve the composite's mechanical integrity under irradiation.
Relative to an otherwise comparable uncoated W–Cu composite, the WC-coated composite will exhibit a statistically significant increase in effective thermal conductivity.
The increase in thermal conductivity will occur without sacrificing mechanical strength.
The increase in thermal conductivity will occur without sacrificing irradiation resistance.
The proposed benefit depends on the WC coating remaining intact during copper infiltration and subsequent thermal and irradiation exposure.
